content.content:
1	# Job logs — every job's full record, retrievable, and retryable from it
2	
3	**Status**: Draft
4	**Created**: 2026-10-07
5	**Supersedes**: nothing
6	**Decision ref**: pending (set when the owner flips this to Active)
7	
8	## Goal
9	
10	Every job leaves a durable record of everything it did, so an operator can
11	read it after the fact and a failed job can be finished later. Each job has an
12	ID. Its record is stored as JSON on the machine that ran it, can be pulled as
13	JSON or as readable text, holds everything a `-p -v` run would have shown plus
14	the internal detail forensics needs, and holds enough to run the job again:
15	`blit retry <job-id>` or `blit retry <path-to-json>` re-runs a failed job on
16	the machine where it originally ran.
17	
18	Requirements as the owner stated them (2026-10-07, verbatim):
19	
20	- R1: "daemon logs need to be retrievable. stored locally in json, with a json
21	  to txt converter option so the user can pull either format. that means job
22	  IDs. this could spiral, so start small."
23	- R2: "saved logs should contain everything a -p -v run would show, plus
24	  whatever internal stuff is needed, and anything else useful for forensics."
25	- R3: "jobs should be retryable if failed via another run, so blit retry
26	  <jobid> or <path_to_json>. finished jobs' json files therefore need to store
27	  what's needed for a retry."
28	- R4: "this should probably be limited to the original machine to avoid the
29	  footgun."
30	
31	Shaping, same day (the owner thinking aloud, then ruling):
32	
33	- Brainstorm: save jobs, local or daemon, "in the same .json format as the
34	  retry jobs, then we can do a blit job <job.json> or something like that",
35	  with every daemon run stored as "a job_run-<timestamp>.log or similar for
36	  retries"; then "we need a way to manage jobs, prune old ones, etc. saving
37	  every local run by default seems like a burden. simplify it for me."
38	- R5 (rejecting "only failed local runs leave a record"): "no. successful
39	  runs are pretty likely to be reused. backup tasks, stuff like that. I think
40	  we need a --save <jobname> and a --export that takes a job ID and works
41	  in-line with --save to save it to the .blit folder internally and export to
42	  the filename specified. that needs to be cleaned up, but you get the idea."
43	- R6: "daemon logs need to live on both daemons, or log hunting will be
44	  annoying."
45	- R7 (retention): "50 default, blit.conf option for others".
46	- R8 (rejecting a two-command surface and dropping saved jobs): "no, result
47	  of above." — saved, reusable jobs are in scope.
48	- R9 (where settings and job files live): "config can't be in /etc because
49	  this is also a windows app. toml is fine, details are up to you. ~/.blit is
50	  universal, or we can use the userprofile to keep it in AppData\Local,
51	  ~/Library/Application Support, etc."
52	
53	Agent's design call under R9's delegation (2026-10-07): one per-user folder
54	per machine, the platform's own — macOS `~/Library/Application
55	Support/com.Blit.Blit` and Linux `~/.config/blit` (the folders
56	`config_dir()` already resolves, holding `recents.jsonl` and the perf
57	history), and Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Blit` (moved from the roaming
58	`%APPDATA%\Blit\Blit\config` `config_dir()` returns today, because job
59	records can be large and a roaming profile copies them at every sign-in; the
60	existing small files move with it once). Inside it: `config.toml` (settings,
61	e.g. how many run records to keep), `jobs/runs/` (run records) and
62	`jobs/saved/` (saved jobs). The daemon keeps its existing machine-wide
63	`config.toml` (`/etc/blit/config.toml` on Linux/macOS,
64	`C:\ProgramData\Blit\config.toml` on Windows — Windows is already covered)
65	for its own settings, and its job records beside its existing recents.
66	
67	- R10 (settings format): "toml if it makes sense. that is up to you. if json
68	  is simpler, fine". Agent's call: TOML for the settings file — a person
69	  edits it, TOML allows comments, and the daemon's settings are already TOML
70	  (one format for both); JSON for run records and saved jobs — machine-
71	  written, and the format the owner asked records to be stored in (R1).
72	- R11 (on the proposed `blit jobs export`): "also needs an in-line --export
73	  that works with --save to save it locally and exported." Owner's question
74	  on the proposed `blit retry`: "why not jobs retry?" (answered in Design).
75	- R12 (confirming the command surface): "right, then we can have a blit jobs
76	  --help for specific help. we should have that same syntax for all verbs.
77	  Yes." Verified 2026-10-07: every verb and sub-verb already answers
78	  `--help` with its own help (clap); the new `jobs` sub-verbs inherit it.
79	  `blit jobs`'s one-line help ("Inspect transfer jobs on a remote daemon")
80	  must change to cover local jobs.
81	- R13 (correcting the proposal that a daemon job could be retried from
82	  anywhere): "no, JOBS are local. LOGS are both. sorry that was unclear."
83	- R14 (what a log holds, after seeing that blit's `-v` lists no files, only a
84	  few diagnostic lines): "okay, so keep -v. drop -p unless that is relevant
85	  forensically".
86	- R15 (Q6, naming files): "B" — a log names every file copied, deleted, and
87	  failed.
88	- R16 (Q7): "store logs compressed."
89	
90	## Non-goals
91	
92	- Spiralling scope (R1: "start small"): the first slices deliver the record,
93	  its retrieval and `blit retry`; anything beyond that waits for its own
94	  ruling.
95	- A new user-visible option the owner did not ask for (repo rule): the owner
96	  asked for `blit retry` and for pulling a log as JSON or text; any other
97	  knob is hidden or worked out at runtime.
98	
99	## Constraints
100	
101	- FAST, SIMPLE, RELIABLE (D-2026-07-09-1): writing the record must not slow a
102	  transfer measurably; the user-facing surface stays the commands the owner
103	  asked for.
104	- Retry runs only on the machine where the job originally ran (R4).
105	- Wire changes land under contract 7 (unreleased; v0.1.3 is contract 6), per
106	  SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT's Constraints, and nothing ships until the open work
107	  is done (D-2026-10-07-3).
108	
109	## Facts this builds on (verified 2026-10-07)
110	
111	- Every daemon job already has an ID (`transfer_id`), shown by `--detach` and
112	  `blit jobs list`; `blit jobs watch` and `blit jobs cancel` take it.
113	- The daemon already persists its last 50 finished jobs as JSON lines
114	  (`recents.jsonl` in its config dir, `crates/blit-daemon/src/recents_store.rs`),
115	  but each record (`TransferRecord`) holds only ok/failed, bytes, files and a
116	  whole-job error message — no per-file failures and no log.
117	- Defect (c) of 2026-10-07 (STATE): a `--detach` job whose files failed one by
118	  one is recorded ok, and `blit jobs watch` reports success. A job record that
119	  carries the failures closes it.
120	- There is no `blit.conf` and no `.blit` folder today. The daemon reads a TOML
121	  config (`/etc/blit/config.toml`, `C:\ProgramData\Blit\config.toml`;
122	  `docs/DAEMON_CONFIG.md`); the CLI has no config file, only its per-user
123	  data folder (`blit_core::config::config_dir()`: `~/Library/Application
124	  Support/com.Blit.Blit` on macOS, `~/.config/blit` on Linux), which already
125	  holds `recents.jsonl` and the perf history. R7's "blit.conf" and R5's
126	  ".blit folder" map onto these unless the owner rules otherwise.
127	
128	## Acceptance criteria
129	
130	- [ ] A `--detach` remote-to-remote job with one file that fails on its own:
131	      `blit jobs watch` exits non-zero and names the file; `blit jobs list`
132	      shows a failed-file count; `blit jobs log <host> <job-id>` shows the
133	      file and its reason (closes defect (c) of 2026-10-07).
134	- [ ] Every run — local copy, push, pull, remote-to-remote — leaves a log on
135	      each machine involved, all under one job ID; `blit jobs log` reads each
136	      as text and, with `--json`, as the raw events.
137	- [ ] A log names every file copied, deleted and failed (with reasons), holds
138	      what `-v` adds, phase start/end times and stall notices; it is written
139	      as the run goes and stored compressed.
140	- [ ] Retention: with the default, the 51st run's log replaces the oldest;
141	      the `config.toml` value is honored; saved jobs are never removed by it.
142	- [ ] `--save <name>`, `--export <file>`, `blit jobs save|export|run|delete|list`
143	      behave as the Design's command surface says; `blit jobs run <name>`
144	      re-runs the same transfer.
145	- [ ] `blit jobs retry <job-id|file>` re-sends only the files that failed,
146	      with the original options; on another machine it refuses with a plain
147	      message naming the machine the job belongs to.
148	- [ ] Windows keeps settings, jobs and logs under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Blit`; files
149	      found in the old roaming folder are moved once.
150	- [ ] FAST: logging costs no measurable slowdown on the existing small-file
151	      and large-file benches (within run-to-run noise).
152	- [ ] Every new sub-verb answers `--help` with its own help (R12).
153	
154	## Design
155	
156	### Command surface (confirmed by the owner 2026-10-07, R12)
157	
158	Two kinds of saved file, one JSON format: **run records** (written by every
159	run on every machine involved, newest 50 kept, R5/R6/R7) and **saved jobs**
160	(written only on request, kept until deleted).
161	
162	1. `blit copy|mirror|move … --save <name>` — run it and keep it as a saved
163	   job `<name>` in the per-user folder.
164	2. `blit copy|mirror|move … --export <file>` — run it and also write its job
165	   to `<file>`; with `--save`, both (R11).
166	3. `blit jobs save <job-id> <name>` — keep a past run as a saved job.
167	4. `blit jobs export <job-id|name> <file>` — write a run record or saved job
168	   to a file.
169	5. `blit jobs run <name|file>` — run a saved job again.
170	6. `blit jobs retry <job-id|file>` — re-send only what failed. Moved under
171	   `jobs` from R3's `blit retry` on the owner's question ("why not jobs
172	   retry?"): every job action then lives under `jobs`, and it cannot be
173	   confused with the transfer flags `--retry`/`--retries`.
174	7. `blit jobs log [<host>] <job-id>` — show a record as text; `--json` for
175	   the raw file.
176	8. `blit jobs list [<host>]`, `blit jobs delete <name>`.
177	
178	### Jobs and logs (R13)
179	
180	- A **job** — what to run again, and how its last run ended (outcome and the
181	  exact failed paths) — lives only on the machine where the command was
182	  typed. `jobs save`, `jobs export`, `jobs run` and `jobs retry` act there and
183	  nowhere else (R4). A remote-to-remote job's failed paths already come back
184	  to the CLI in the delegated summary (`failed_paths`, exact), so its local
185	  job holds them. Proposed for a `--detach` job, whose CLI exits before the
186	  outcome exists: `jobs retry` fetches the outcome by job ID from the
187	  receiving daemon's log, then re-runs from this machine.
188	- A **log** — the forensic record of everything a `-p -v` run would show plus
189	  internal detail (R2) — is kept by every machine that took part, each for
190	  its own part, under the same job ID: the local machine for a local copy;
191	  the CLI machine and the daemon for a push or pull; both daemons for a
192	  remote-to-remote job (R6), and the CLI machine for what it saw.
193	  `blit jobs log [<host>] <job-id>` reads any of them.
194	
195	### What a log holds (R2, R14)
196	
197	- The run's identity: job ID, machine, verb, source, destination, options,
198	  start and end time, and the outcome.
199	- Everything `-v` adds today, whether or not `-v` was given: scan time,
200	  average rate, workers used, the planned count and bytes, and how files
201	  were batched (verified 2026-10-07: blit's `-v` lists no file names).
202	- The final summary: counts of files copied, deleted, failed; bytes.
203	- Every failed file with its reason.
204	- From `-p`, only what answers after the fact where time went (agent's call
205	  under R14): when each phase (scan, transfer, delete) started and ended, and
206	  any stall notice. The redrawn progress line and periodic progress
207	  snapshots are not kept.
208	- Every file copied and every file deleted, by name (R15).
209	- Size (agent's design, follows from R15): a million-file backup's log is
210	  on the order of 100 MB, and 50 are kept per machine. The log is written to
211	  disk as the run goes — one JSON event per line — never held in memory, so
212	  a large job costs disk, not RAM, and is compressed when the run finishes
213	  (R16). `blit jobs log` reads it as text or JSON transparently; `blit jobs
214	  export` writes it uncompressed.
215	
216	### Identity, protocol and retention (agent's design within the rulings)
217	
218	- **Job ID.** The machine where the command is typed creates the ID (a
219	  random 128-bit ID shown in short form, like `--detach` shows today) and
220	  sends it with the transfer, so every machine involved logs under the same
221	  ID. A daemon still creates one for a job no CLI started.
222	- **Machine ID.** Created once per machine and kept in the per-user folder;
223	  every job records it, and `blit jobs retry`/`run` refuse a job whose ID is
224	  not this machine's (R4). Hostnames change, so they are not used.
225	- **Protocol (contract 7, unreleased).** The job ID rides the session-open
226	  and delegated-pull requests; a new `GetJobLog` call returns one log by ID;
227	  the finished-job record (`TransferRecord`) gains the failed-file count.
228	- **Retention.** Per machine, the newest 50 logs and the newest 50 run
229	  records (R7) — `[jobs] keep = 50` in the CLI's new per-user `config.toml`
230	  and in the daemon's existing `config.toml`. Saved jobs are kept until
231	  deleted. Pruning happens when a run finishes; nothing to manage.
232	- **Exposure.** A daemon's logs name files; `blit jobs log <host>` reads them
233	  with the same reach `blit ls`/`find` already have on that daemon — no new
234	  access.
235	
236	## Slices
237	
238	Small first, per R1; each slice is one coherent, testable change.
239	
240	1. **jl-1 — daemon logs (the small start).** The daemon writes each job's
241	   log (identity, `-v` diagnostics, phase times and stalls, every copied,
242	   deleted and failed file) as it runs, compressed when it ends, keeps the
243	   newest 50 (`[jobs] keep` in its `config.toml`); `GetJobLog`; `blit jobs log
244	   <host> <job-id> [--json]`; `jobs list`/`watch` show the failed-file count
245	   and `watch` exits non-zero when files failed (closes defect (c)).
246	2. **jl-2 — one job ID everywhere, local logs.** The CLI creates the job ID and
247	   sends it, so both daemons of a remote-to-remote job and the CLI machine log
248	   under it; local runs write logs too; the per-user folder (Windows moved to
249	   `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Blit`, old files moved once), the CLI's `config.toml`;
250	   `blit jobs log <job-id|file>` and `blit jobs list` locally.
251	3. **jl-3 — jobs.** Every run writes its job (what to run, how it ended,
252	   exact failed paths) locally; machine ID; `--save`, `--export`, `blit jobs
253	   save|export|run|delete`.
254	4. **jl-4 — retry.** `blit jobs retry <job-id|file>`: re-send only the failed
255	   paths with the original options, through the existing retry-pass
256	   machinery; refuse on another machine; a `--detach` job's outcome fetched
257	   by ID from the receiving daemon's log.
258	
259	## Open questions
260	
261	Asked one at a time, in this order:
262	
263	- Q1. Which runs write a job record? — RULED by R5/R6: every run (a
264	  successful run is likely reused); every machine involved in a job keeps it
265	  — for remote-to-remote, both daemons (R6).

# Job logs — every job's full record, retrievable, and retryable from it

**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-10-07
**Supersedes**: nothing
**Decision ref**: pending (set when the owner flips this to Active)

## Goal

Every job leaves a durable record of everything it did, so an operator can
read it after the fact and a failed job can be finished later. Each job has an
ID. Its record is stored as JSON on the machine that ran it, can be pulled as
JSON or as readable text, holds everything a `-p -v` run would have shown plus
the internal detail forensics needs, and holds enough to run the job again:
`blit retry <job-id>` or `blit retry <path-to-json>` re-runs a failed job on
the machine where it originally ran.

Requirements as the owner stated them (2026-10-07, verbatim):

- R1: "daemon logs need to be retrievable. stored locally in json, with a json
  to txt converter option so the user can pull either format. that means job
  IDs. this could spiral, so start small."
- R2: "saved logs should contain everything a -p -v run would show, plus
  whatever internal stuff is needed, and anything else useful for forensics."
- R3: "jobs should be retryable if failed via another run, so blit retry
  <jobid> or <path_to_json>. finished jobs' json files therefore need to store
  what's needed for a retry."
- R4: "this should probably be limited to the original machine to avoid the
  footgun."

Shaping, same day (the owner thinking aloud, then ruling):

- Brainstorm: save jobs, local or daemon, "in the same .json format as the
  retry jobs, then we can do a blit job <job.json> or something like that",
  with every daemon run stored as "a job_run-<timestamp>.log or similar for
  retries"; then "we need a way to manage jobs, prune old ones, etc. saving
  every local run by default seems like a burden. simplify it for me."
- R5 (rejecting "only failed local runs leave a record"): "no. successful
  runs are pretty likely to be reused. backup tasks, stuff like that. I think
  we need a --save <jobname> and a --export that takes a job ID and works
  in-line with --save to save it to the .blit folder internally and export to
  the filename specified. that needs to be cleaned up, but you get the idea."
- R6: "daemon logs need to live on both daemons, or log hunting will be
  annoying."
- R7 (retention): "50 default, blit.conf option for others".
- R8 (rejecting a two-command surface and dropping saved jobs): "no, result
  of above." — saved, reusable jobs are in scope.
- R9 (where settings and job files live): "config can't be in /etc because
  this is also a windows app. toml is fine, details are up to you. ~/.blit is
  universal, or we can use the userprofile to keep it in AppData\Local,
  ~/Library/Application Support, etc."

Agent's design call under R9's delegation (2026-10-07): one per-user folder
per machine, the platform's own — macOS `~/Library/Application
Support/com.Blit.Blit` and Linux `~/.config/blit` (the folders
`config_dir()` already resolves, holding `recents.jsonl` and the perf
history), and Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Blit` (moved from the roaming
`%APPDATA%\Blit\Blit\config` `config_dir()` returns today, because job
records can be large and a roaming profile copies them at every sign-in; the
existing small files move with it once). Inside it: `config.toml` (settings,
e.g. how many run records to keep), `jobs/runs/` (run records) and
`jobs/saved/` (saved jobs). The daemon keeps its existing machine-wide
`config.toml` (`/etc/blit/config.toml` on Linux/macOS,
`C:\ProgramData\Blit\config.toml` on Windows — Windows is already covered)
for its own settings, and its job records beside its existing recents.

- R10 (settings format): "toml if it makes sense. that is up to you. if json
  is simpler, fine". Agent's call: TOML for the settings file — a person
  edits it, TOML allows comments, and the daemon's settings are already TOML
  (one format for both); JSON for run records and saved jobs — machine-
  written, and the format the owner asked records to be stored in (R1).
- R11 (on the proposed `blit jobs export`): "also needs an in-line --export
  that works with --save to save it locally and exported." Owner's question
  on the proposed `blit retry`: "why not jobs retry?" (answered in Design).
- R12 (confirming the command surface): "right, then we can have a blit jobs
  --help for specific help. we should have that same syntax for all verbs.
  Yes." Verified 2026-10-07: every verb and sub-verb already answers
  `--help` with its own help (clap); the new `jobs` sub-verbs inherit it.
  `blit jobs`'s one-line help ("Inspect transfer jobs on a remote daemon")
  must change to cover local jobs.
- R13 (correcting the proposal that a daemon job could be retried from
  anywhere): "no, JOBS are local. LOGS are both. sorry that was unclear."
- R14 (what a log holds, after seeing that blit's `-v` lists no files, only a
  few diagnostic lines): "okay, so keep -v. drop -p unless that is relevant
  forensically".
- R15 (Q6, naming files): "B" — a log names every file copied, deleted, and
  failed.
- R16 (Q7): "store logs compressed."

## Non-goals

- Spiralling scope (R1: "start small"): the first slices deliver the record,
  its retrieval and `blit retry`; anything beyond that waits for its own
  ruling.
- A new user-visible option the owner did not ask for (repo rule): the owner
  asked for `blit retry` and for pulling a log as JSON or text; any other
  knob is hidden or worked out at runtime.

## Constraints

- FAST, SIMPLE, RELIABLE (D-2026-07-09-1): writing the record must not slow a
  transfer measurably; the user-facing surface stays the commands the owner
  asked for.
- Retry runs only on the machine where the job originally ran (R4).
- Wire changes land under contract 7 (unreleased; v0.1.3 is contract 6), per
  SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT's Constraints, and nothing ships until the open work
  is done (D-2026-10-07-3).

## Facts this builds on (verified 2026-10-07)

- Every daemon job already has an ID (`transfer_id`), shown by `--detach` and
  `blit jobs list`; `blit jobs watch` and `blit jobs cancel` take it.
- The daemon already persists its last 50 finished jobs as JSON lines
  (`recents.jsonl` in its config dir, `crates/blit-daemon/src/recents_store.rs`),
  but each record (`TransferRecord`) holds only ok/failed, bytes, files and a
  whole-job error message — no per-file failures and no log.
- Defect (c) of 2026-10-07 (STATE): a `--detach` job whose files failed one by
  one is recorded ok, and `blit jobs watch` reports success. A job record that
  carries the failures closes it.
- There is no `blit.conf` and no `.blit` folder today. The daemon reads a TOML
  config (`/etc/blit/config.toml`, `C:\ProgramData\Blit\config.toml`;
  `docs/DAEMON_CONFIG.md`); the CLI has no config file, only its per-user
  data folder (`blit_core::config::config_dir()`: `~/Library/Application
  Support/com.Blit.Blit` on macOS, `~/.config/blit` on Linux), which already
  holds `recents.jsonl` and the perf history. R7's "blit.conf" and R5's
  ".blit folder" map onto these unless the owner rules otherwise.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `--detach` remote-to-remote job with one file that fails on its own:
      `blit jobs watch` exits non-zero and names the file; `blit jobs list`
      shows a failed-file count; `blit jobs log <host> <job-id>` shows the
      file and its reason (closes defect (c) of 2026-10-07).
- [ ] Every run — local copy, push, pull, remote-to-remote — leaves a log on
      each machine involved, all under one job ID; `blit jobs log` reads each
      as text and, with `--json`, as the raw events.
- [ ] A log names every file copied, deleted and failed (with reasons), holds
      what `-v` adds, phase start/end times and stall notices; it is written
      as the run goes and stored compressed.
- [ ] Retention: with the default, the 51st run's log replaces the oldest;
      the `config.toml` value is honored; saved jobs are never removed by it.
- [ ] `--save <name>`, `--export <file>`, `blit jobs save|export|run|delete|list`
      behave as the Design's command surface says; `blit jobs run <name>`
      re-runs the same transfer.
- [ ] `blit jobs retry <job-id|file>` re-sends only the files that failed,
      with the original options; on another machine it refuses with a plain
      message naming the machine the job belongs to.
- [ ] Windows keeps settings, jobs and logs under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Blit`; files
      found in the old roaming folder are moved once.
- [ ] FAST: logging costs no measurable slowdown on the existing small-file
      and large-file benches (within run-to-run noise).
- [ ] Every new sub-verb answers `--help` with its own help (R12).

## Design

### Command surface (confirmed by the owner 2026-10-07, R12)

Two kinds of saved file, one JSON format: **run records** (written by every
run on every machine involved, newest 50 kept, R5/R6/R7) and **saved jobs**
(written only on request, kept until deleted).

1. `blit copy|mirror|move … --save <name>` — run it and keep it as a saved
   job `<name>` in the per-user folder.
2. `blit copy|mirror|move … --export <file>` — run it and also write its job
   to `<file>`; with `--save`, both (R11).
3. `blit jobs save <job-id> <name>` — keep a past run as a saved job.
4. `blit jobs export <job-id|name> <file>` — write a run record or saved job
   to a file.
5. `blit jobs run <name|file>` — run a saved job again.
6. `blit jobs retry <job-id|file>` — re-send only what failed. Moved under
   `jobs` from R3's `blit retry` on the owner's question ("why not jobs
   retry?"): every job action then lives under `jobs`, and it cannot be
   confused with the transfer flags `--retry`/`--retries`.
7. `blit jobs log [<host>] <job-id>` — show a record as text; `--json` for
   the raw file.
8. `blit jobs list [<host>]`, `blit jobs delete <name>`.

### Jobs and logs (R13)

- A **job** — what to run again, and how its last run ended (outcome and the
  exact failed paths) — lives only on the machine where the command was
  typed. `jobs save`, `jobs export`, `jobs run` and `jobs retry` act there and
  nowhere else (R4). A remote-to-remote job's failed paths already come back
  to the CLI in the delegated summary (`failed_paths`, exact), so its local
  job holds them. Proposed for a `--detach` job, whose CLI exits before the
  outcome exists: `jobs retry` fetches the outcome by job ID from the
  receiving daemon's log, then re-runs from this machine.
- A **log** — the forensic record of everything a `-p -v` run would show plus
  internal detail (R2) — is kept by every machine that took part, each for
  its own part, under the same job ID: the local machine for a local copy;
  the CLI machine and the daemon for a push or pull; both daemons for a
  remote-to-remote job (R6), and the CLI machine for what it saw.
  `blit jobs log [<host>] <job-id>` reads any of them.

### What a log holds (R2, R14)

- The run's identity: job ID, machine, verb, source, destination, options,
  start and end time, and the outcome.
- Everything `-v` adds today, whether or not `-v` was given: scan time,
  average rate, workers used, the planned count and bytes, and how files
  were batched (verified 2026-10-07: blit's `-v` lists no file names).
- The final summary: counts of files copied, deleted, failed; bytes.
- Every failed file with its reason.
- From `-p`, only what answers after the fact where time went (agent's call
  under R14): when each phase (scan, transfer, delete) started and ended, and
  any stall notice. The redrawn progress line and periodic progress
  snapshots are not kept.
- Every file copied and every file deleted, by name (R15).
- Size (agent's design, follows from R15): a million-file backup's log is
  on the order of 100 MB, and 50 are kept per machine. The log is written to
  disk as the run goes — one JSON event per line — never held in memory, so
  a large job costs disk, not RAM, and is compressed when the run finishes
  (R16). `blit jobs log` reads it as text or JSON transparently; `blit jobs
  export` writes it uncompressed.

### Identity, protocol and retention (agent's design within the rulings)

- **Job ID.** The machine where the command is typed creates the ID (a
  random 128-bit ID shown in short form, like `--detach` shows today) and
  sends it with the transfer, so every machine involved logs under the same
  ID. A daemon still creates one for a job no CLI started.
- **Machine ID.** Created once per machine and kept in the per-user folder;
  every job records it, and `blit jobs retry`/`run` refuse a job whose ID is
  not this machine's (R4). Hostnames change, so they are not used.
- **Protocol (contract 7, unreleased).** The job ID rides the session-open
  and delegated-pull requests; a new `GetJobLog` call returns one log by ID;
  the finished-job record (`TransferRecord`) gains the failed-file count.
- **Retention.** Per machine, the newest 50 logs and the newest 50 run
  records (R7) — `[jobs] keep = 50` in the CLI's new per-user `config.toml`
  and in the daemon's existing `config.toml`. Saved jobs are kept until
  deleted. Pruning happens when a run finishes; nothing to manage.
- **Exposure.** A daemon's logs name files; `blit jobs log <host>` reads them
  with the same reach `blit ls`/`find` already have on that daemon — no new
  access.

## Slices

Small first, per R1; each slice is one coherent, testable change.

1. **jl-1 — daemon logs (the small start).** The daemon writes each job's
   log (identity, `-v` diagnostics, phase times and stalls, every copied,
   deleted and failed file) as it runs, compressed when it ends, keeps the
   newest 50 (`[jobs] keep` in its `config.toml`); `GetJobLog`; `blit jobs log
   <host> <job-id> [--json]`; `jobs list`/`watch` show the failed-file count
   and `watch` exits non-zero when files failed (closes defect (c)).
2. **jl-2 — one job ID everywhere, local logs.** The CLI creates the job ID and
   sends it, so both daemons of a remote-to-remote job and the CLI machine log
   under it; local runs write logs too; the per-user folder (Windows moved to
   `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Blit`, old files moved once), the CLI's `config.toml`;
   `blit jobs log <job-id|file>` and `blit jobs list` locally.
3. **jl-3 — jobs.** Every run writes its job (what to run, how it ended,
   exact failed paths) locally; machine ID; `--save`, `--export`, `blit jobs
   save|export|run|delete`.
4. **jl-4 — retry.** `blit jobs retry <job-id|file>`: re-send only the failed
   paths with the original options, through the existing retry-pass
   machinery; refuse on another machine; a `--detach` job's outcome fetched
   by ID from the receiving daemon's log.

## Open questions

Asked one at a time, in this order:

- Q1. Which runs write a job record? — RULED by R5/R6: every run (a
  successful run is likely reused); every machine involved in a job keeps it
  — for remote-to-remote, both daemons (R6).
- Q2. Which machine re-runs a job — RULED (R13): jobs are local to the
  machine where the command was typed; logs live on every machine involved.
- Q3. What a retry re-runs — RULED with the command surface (R12):
  `blit jobs retry` re-sends only what failed, with the original options;
  `blit jobs run` re-runs a whole saved job.
- Q4. How long records are kept — RULED by R7: the last 50 by default,
  configurable in `config.toml` (R9: TOML, per-user folder; the daemon's in
  its own `config.toml`). A saved job does not count toward the 50 — it is
  kept until deleted (proposed with the command surface, confirmed R12).
- Q5. The cleaned-up command surface — RULED (R12): see Design.
- Q6. Whether a log names files — RULED (R15): every file copied, deleted
  and failed.
- Q7. Compress finished logs — RULED (R16): yes.
